news.title: 14 Trends in AI Monetization
news.gist: Drawing on Teneo research, Litterst sorts 14 AI monetization trends into settled, emerging and frontier groups: mixing a fixed fee with usage is now standard, while credits, wallets and outcome pricing are still being worked out.
points: Seats lose ground because the better an agent works, the fewer people a customer needs on the product
Buyers take variable bills only with structure, as in Salesforce Pre-Commit, Workday Flex Credits and SAP AI Units
Credits can track vendor cost, product activity or finished work; the last holds up best but needs a clear definition of done
Most vendors fold MCP access into existing plans, and separate MCP add-ons are still rare
nums: vendors pairing a fixed fee with a usage charge, up from 45% in 2023

news.why: Before signing a usage or credit deal, ask for the commitment tiers and spending controls the piece says buyers now expect, so the bill can’t run open-ended.

news.title: Pricing Changes: September 21–27, 2026
news.gist: Developer free tiers mostly got tighter this week: Svix, AppSignal, Nango and Pulumi trimmed free allowances and Stickies dropped its free plan, while Railway and Browserless gave a little more away.
points: OpenAI shut down Sora 2 video generation in its API and Groq retired its Compound models, neither naming a replacement
Svix moved its uptime SLA off the Free plan and into a paid Basic plan
Storj now takes USDC instead of its own token for bill deposits and ended the token deposit discount
Fireworks AI pulled several DeepSeek, GLM and Kimi models from serverless; dedicated deployments are unaffected
nums: monthly requests on AppSignal’s Free plan, down from 50,000
5M
free Neo tokens a month Pulumi removed from its free plan
Pulumi’s Neo price per 1M tokens, now on paid plans only
2 minutes
Browserless Free plan session limit, up from 1 minute
news.why: If a project runs on a developer tool’s free tier, recheck its limits now, since several shrank this week with no change to the paid plans.

news.title: Developer Tool Pricing Report: September 2026
news.gist: AgentDeals’ September count of developer-tool pricing moves ran heavily against buyers, with retirements and reduced limits far outnumbering gains such as Railway’s free VM and Cloudflare Workers’ larger size limit.
points: CockroachDB ended its free Basic plan for new deployments and offers a credit-backed trial instead
OneSignal limited free mobile push to organizations below a monthly-active-user ceiling
Modal’s Starter compute allowance no longer covers Shared Endpoints, which are billed from the first request
AI and ML logged the most changes of any category, and none of them were positive
nums: developer-tool pricing changes logged in September
negative changes, against 3 positive

news.why: Budget for developer tools as if free tiers will keep shrinking, and check which services in your stack were retired or capped in September.

news.title: Airtable reverses its own automations cap two days after imposing it, tiering 75-200 by plan
news.gist: Airtable swapped the flat automations-per-base cap it had set days earlier for a plan-by-plan schedule, and PricingSaaS reads the speed of the U-turn as a correction after the cap hit paying teams too hard.
points: The same limit changed three times in four days: floated on 26 Sep, set again on 28 Sep and loosened on 30 Sep
Paid plans get the biggest increases over the flat cap, and Free the smallest
Airtable gave no reason, and the article argues reversals this fast follow usage data or pushback, not a planned test
That kind of churn can make automation-heavy teams wary of building more on the platform
nums: flat automations-per-base cap set on 28 Sep
new cap on Enterprise Scale, with 75 on Free, 100 on Team and 150 on Business
days in Airtable’s usual gap between pricing changes
news.why: If your workflows depend on a per-base limit, check the cap your plan now has, and don’t design around a number that changed three times in a week.

patterns.t: AI gets its own allowance or plan
patterns.p: Seat-priced products gave AI a separate monthly allowance or a plan of its own instead of raising the seat price, so the size of the allowance becomes the real price lever. Teamwork.com’s delay shows the switch isn’t always smooth.

points.text: made “AI in Dropbox” live on Standard and Advanced with 250 and 750 AI credits a month
added monthly AI credit allowances of 1,000 to 6,000 by plan to one app’s restructured plans

patterns.t: Caps appear where plans had none
patterns.p: Several vendors put a number on allowances they used to sell as unlimited or uncapped, which pushes heavy users toward a bigger plan or Enterprise. Airtable reversed its cap within days, a sign the first number can be wrong. Tavus, Foreplay and Flockler come from PricingSaaS reports.

patterns.t: Prices rebuilt around a new unit
patterns.p: Vendors changed what they count, moving to credits, cloud accounts, sites, agent-months or a revenue share. A new unit can raise or lower a bill with no change to a headline price, so rerun your own volumes. Snyk, Nacelle, Hudu and Domotz come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.figNote: changes that repackage rather than raise or lower what buyers pay
stats_analysis.p: The rest split 40 that cost buyers more against 23 that saved them money. Repackaging ranged from Dropbox’s AI credits and Zoho’s per-plan allowances to new billing units at Snyk and SparkPost. Most of the week’s records come from PricingSaaS reports, so the mix partly reflects what its feeds showed.

stats_analysis.t: A third of the week involved AI
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that touch AI features or AI pricing
stats_analysis.p: AI changes ran both ways. Anthropic launched a cheaper flagship and Kurrent and Zenzap moved AI features down to cheaper plans, while Synthesia cut Basic’s AI video assets and Oneflow turned AI review into a paid add-on. Six of the AI changes moved features between tiers.

stats_analysis.t: Limits loosened more often than they tightened
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that loosen vs tighten a limit
stats_analysis.p: Looser limits were mostly small and technical, and 18 of the 20 came from smaller companies, such as Expo’s subrequests, ToolJet’s app counts, Kapwing’s storage and Hedra’s credits. Tighter ones reached bigger names: 4 of the 16 changes rated relevant tightened a limit, at Airtable, Cognition, Supabase and Synthesia. About half the loosened limits come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: Thirteen vendors changed what they bill for
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that switch to a new billing unit
stats_analysis.p: Snyk moved Enterprise to credits, Prowler to cloud accounts, Lyzr from agent runs to agent-month subscriptions and Domotz from devices to sites, while Nacelle added a revenue share. All 13 came from smaller companies, outside the week’s relevant list; Snyk, Nacelle, Domotz, Postman and Picsart come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: The relevant changes split almost evenly
stats_analysis.p: Six cost buyers more, five saved them money and five repackaged. The cuts include Anthropic’s cheaper flagship and Intercom’s cheaper Essential seat, which later proved to be a price test; four of the six rises are tighter limits, at Airtable, Cognition, Supabase and Synthesia. Intercom, Baremetrics, Render, beehiiv and ExpressVPN come from PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.figNote: changes classed as price increases vs price cuts
stats_analysis.p: Ten of the 11 increases came from smaller companies, among them Vista Social, 7shifts, Draxlr and Luzmo. Cuts reached the top of the market too, with 2 from market leaders, Anthropic and Intercom, while Baremetrics and Bettermode made the deepest plan-price cuts. Most of these increases and cuts come from PricingSaaS reports.

news_trends.t: Credits become the default way to sell AI
news_trends.p: Good Better Best calls hybrid fixed-plus-usage pricing the norm and credits the emerging common currency, with wallets and spending controls becoming part of the product. This week’s records match: Dropbox and Zoho added monthly AI credit allowances, Snyk moved Enterprise to credits and Hedra raised plan credits. No earlier editions are in this edition’s window, so the theme rests on this week’s stories.
nums: vendors pairing a fixed fee with a usage charge, up from 45% in 2023

news_trends.p: AgentDeals’ weekly digest and its September report both show developer free tiers losing limits, features or the free plan itself. Outside developer tools our records show the same thing: Sendcloud stopped free-plan overage, Regie.ai took its dialer off Free and Exa cut first-month free credits, the last two from PricingSaaS reports.

news_trends.t: Buyers want predictable bills, and fast-moving limits undercut them
news_trends.p: Good Better Best finds unpredictable pricing a bigger reason to reject AI features than a high price. Airtable showed the other side, changing one limit three times in four days, while Teamwork.com delayed its AI credit billing and Intercom ran a seat-price test.

news_trends.p: AgentDeals logged model shutdowns with no named replacement at OpenAI and Groq, and Fireworks pulling several models from serverless, with deprecations the most common change in September. In our records Anthropic’s new flagship launched cheaper than the model it replaced, while Crusoe reset fine-tuning prices in both directions.
